LA.title: Louisiana: NGO funding request
LA.status: The question list matches the 2026 NGO request form. Joint Rule 17 details come from search results of the rule's text, and 2025 proposals may have changed it, so confirm the current version.
dates: Requests are due to the House and Senate money committees.
A late request can be included only if the Joint Legislative Committee on the Budget or the Capital Outlay committee approves it first.
items: Decide which funding you need (operating or capital outlay) and find a legislator to carry it
Review La. R.S. 39:51.1 and Joint Rule 17 before starting the form
Entity type, such as nonprofit corporation, and names of the incorporators
Proof of good standing with the Secretary of State, if registered there
Last four digits of the taxpayer ID
Tax exemption status
Names of everyone on the governing board and all officers
Physical and mailing address, and a named contact person
Exact dollar amount, and whether it's a general appropriation, capital outlay, or both
Project or program summary
Budget split into salaries, professional services, contracts, acquisitions, major repairs, operating services and other charges
Public purpose the funds will achieve
Goals and objectives for achieving that purpose
Estimated time to accomplish the purpose
Any outstanding audit issues, and how you're resolving them
Disclosure of any ties or contracts with state officials or their immediate family
notes: Submitting the form is required for consideration but does not guarantee funding.
Completed forms are published online, including board names and addresses, so assume everything you enter becomes public.
Of the 227 requests in 2026, 26 had every named line vetoed, so plan for that risk.

FL.title: Florida: Local Funding Initiative Request
FL.status: Questions below come directly from the FY2026-27 Senate request form. Check the form for the year you are filing, and ask your Senate sponsor's office for the filing window.
dates: Requests go through a Senate sponsor. The Senate posts filed forms on its website each fiscal year.
In 2026 the Governor signed the budget and issued line-item vetoes on June 29. Being in the budget is not final until then.
items: Secure a Senate sponsor (and consider a House member, since funded lines usually cite both chambers)
Project title and a clear project or program description
State agency that would receive the funds, and whether you have contacted it
Amount requested, split between operating and fixed capital outlay
Total project cost, with federal, state, local and other matching funds
Whether the project has received state funding before, and any past veto
Whether future-year funding is likely, and what would replace state money
For construction: phase, permits, start and end dates, how operations will be funded, and who owns the facility
How the state money will be spent, by category, including administration and salaries
Specific purpose or goal the funds will achieve
Activities and direct services for citizens
Target population and how many people will be served
Expected outcome, and how you will measure it
Penalties the contracting agency could apply if you miss deliverables
Any natural disaster link, FEMA worksheet, and other federal or state assistance
Requester, recipient and any lobbyist contact details
notes: Filed forms are public PDFs and include contact details, so use organization contact information.
In FY2026-27, 478 of the 1,854 requests cited in the budget were vetoed, so plan for that risk.

DE.title: Delaware: Grant-in-Aid
DE.status: Requirements and dates below come directly from the Delaware General Assembly's Grant-in-Aid pages.
dates: FY2028 General and Veterans applications close. They opened September 8, 2026.
FY2028 Senior Center application window, closing at 3 pm.
The Joint Finance Committee decides. The bill is historically the last appropriations bill enacted, on June 30.
New eligibility rules from House Bill 190 begin, affecting the FY2029 cycle.
items: Incorporated nonprofit (or under an incorporated parent) operating for two years before applying
Bylaws stating your purpose and the duties of the Board
Active, community-represented, volunteer Board with minutes of its meetings
Programs not duplicated by other state-supported agencies and meeting unmet needs
Personnel policies, including job descriptions and classifications
Non-discrimination practice
Accounting and budget procedures
CPA or Public Accountant audit, review or compilation within the past three years, or a statement and supporting records if you can't comply
Evidence of community support
Program is not fully funded from other revenue
Applying directly, not through a fiscal agent
My.Delaware.gov account for the Grants Management System
For FY2029: conflict-of-interest and whistleblower policies, and at least 50% of operations funded from other sources
notes: Grant-in-Aid can't pay for child daycare, capital equipment, buying or renovating buildings, elected officials' pay, campaigns, lobbying, or services for people outside Delaware.
Application materials can be inspected by the public under FOIA.
